audit_findings.title: The anchor extrapolates an abnormal, non-steady-state year
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.3 million of filed 2025 additional quality-related costs; incentive-compensation offset unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The incident costs reduce 2025 OE and therefore the $0.1 million anchor, while unusually low incentive compensation increases that same anchor; both effects are compounded through forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The unfavorable impacts of lower sales volumes and $27.3 million of additional costs incurred related to the quality issue described above, which consisted of a quality claim, material scrap expenses, and temporary plant idling costs, were partially offset by manufacturing efficiencies and improved margins along with lower incentive compensation expense in 2025 compared to 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the anchor year contained abnormal quality-claim, scrap, and idling costs and depressed incentive compensation. Their net normalization is unresolved, but the $27.3 million adverse component is 273 times the anchor and therefore capable of changing the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2025 OE line by line, separately identify after-tax incident costs, recoveries, recurring remediation costs, and normalized incentive compensation, then rerun all scenarios with the resulting normalized OE disclosed separately from the mandated latest-actual anchor.

audit_findings.title: Cash added to equity may not be wholly surplus cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.987 million added cash; potentially non-surplus portion unquantified; the added cash equals 95.2% of the $21 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any operating, restricted, or covenant-support cash is unavailable for distribution and must be excluded from the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash on hand up to $35.0 million can benefit the covenants and may benefit the borrowing capacity under the Credit Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that cash can support covenants and borrowing capacity, but does not establish the minimum cash that must remain in the business. Because almost the entire modeled equity value comes from the cash addition, even a partial disallowance could materially reduce value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the covenant calculation, minimum operating-cash analysis, subsidiary restrictions, and borrowing-capacity effect of a distribution; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably distributable surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded retirement obligations may be an unmodeled senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.887 million 2025 funded deficit ($13.895 million pension plus $2.992 million other benefits), equal to 80.4% of the $21 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Required contributions reduce future equity-level OE; any deficit not captured by forecast contributions or benefit expense may require a senior-claim deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Significant changes in market interest rates and decreases in the fair value of plan assets and investment losses on plan assets would increase funding requirements and expenses and may adversely impact our results of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The deficits are filed amounts and the bridge contains no explicit retirement adjustment. It remains unresolved whether the OE calculation already captures the economically required contributions, but the recorded deficit is large enough relative to modeled equity value to be material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile historical and forecast cash contributions against OE, obtain the latest funded status by plan, separate funded and unfunded arrangements, and rerun with any residual obligation deducted once rather than double-counted through OE.

audit_findings.title: Customer prepayments can create future earnings without future cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $41.1 million long-term and $1.8 million current customer prepayments at 2026-07-03; the combined balance declined $7.0 million during the first six months of 2026, equal to 33.3% of the $21 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Revenue and profit recognized as prepaid obligations are fulfilled may not produce contemporaneous cash; fulfillment costs and the liability unwind must enter OE working-capital adjustments or the forecast explicitly.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, $47.5 million and $60.9 million, respectively, of prepayments are classified as Unearned income on the Consolidated Balance Sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed balances and $7.0 million six-month unwind demonstrate a material cash-timing exposure, but the record does not show whether the OE engine captured long-term unearned income as well as current unearned revenue. The possible omission is therefore unresolved, not demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Trace both unearned-income and unearned-revenue changes through every historical OE calculation, map future revenue recognition to remaining fulfillment costs and cash receipts, and rerun forecasts excluding profit that lacks incremental cash after fulfillment spending.

audit_findings.title: Mine development is a separate recurring capital requirement
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.288 million paid in 2025 and $1.661 million in the first six months of 2026; the 2025 payment equals 125.2% of the $21 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Economically necessary mine-development cash spending reduces OE independently of conventional property, plant, and equipment purchases; depletion must not substitute for or duplicate the cash deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Mine development costs at our open pit surface mines include drilling, infrastructure, other related costs to delineate an ore body and the removal of overburden to initially expose an ore body.
audit_findings.explanation: The separate cash-flow classification and amount are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE engine included the payments. If omitted, the 2025 overstatement would be material relative to both the $0.1 million anchor and modeled equity value.
audit_findings.action: Audit each historical OE year for a distinct mine-development cash deduction, determine a supportable recurring requirement from filed payments and mine plans, check for duplication with depletion, and rerun the valuation if any year omitted it.

audit_findings.title: Environmental claims extend beyond reliably measurable reserves
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.4 million latest environmental reserve plus $3.045 million 2025 asset-retirement obligation; additional preliminary-site exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Environmental payments and asset-retirement spending reduce OE, while obligations not represented by recurring cash flows may require a separate equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: For sites that are in the preliminary stages of investigation, the ultimate loss contingencies cannot be reasonably determined at the present time.
audit_findings.explanation: Recorded reserves and obligations are concrete, but the filing says preliminary-site losses cannot presently be determined. The record also does not show whether payments, accrual changes, and accretion were fully captured in OE. Consequently, additional value exposure exists, but its materiality cannot be established from the available amounts.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile environmental payments, reserve movements, ARO accretion, and capitalized retirement assets through OE; obtain site-level estimates, timing, insurance coverage, and latest reserves, then rerun or apply a bridge deduction only for obligations not already captured.
